symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1627, second symptom: describe → exec of a view entity re-indented its OQL. Stored text whose every line was indented, or tab-indented, came back flush; a leading blank line, a trailing newline, and a comment before the first or after the last token were dropped — on a statement the user did not change
cause: The parser stores the query from its first token to its last and dedents the shared prefix (#653). Describe indents every stored line by two, so a stored indentation on all lines is indistinguishable from the script's own, and anything outside the token span (whitespace, a blank first line, a hidden-channel comment) has no carrier at all
fix: execCreateViewEntity keeps the STORED query when the statement's query equals what the stored one describes to — computed by rendering it with the describer's own function and parsing that back with visitor.Build — and writes the authored text otherwise
test: TestCreateOrModifyViewEntity_KeepsStoredOQLItDescribes (5 stored shapes on PedApp, each with an edit control that must still land)
insight: **The span of a parse is a lossy channel, so make the carry decision with the real parser, not a model of it**: viewQueryAsReexecuted parses `describedViewQuery(stored)` exactly as a script would and compares, so a future change to dedentOQL or the token span cannot desynchronise the carry. A text-only fix is impossible here — `  select…\n  from…` stored and a script indenting its query by four are the same bytes after describe — which is why it is a carry (statement denotes stored) and not a better dedent. The scratch probe that found the shapes was cheap: feed candidate stored strings through describeEntityToString + parseViewEntityQuery and diff; 7 of 9 drifted. Comments outside the span are still lost on a describe → exec into a FRESH project (no stored text to carry) — a grammar question, not fixed here
